subject: flame lighter
title: The Lighter Was Invented 3 Years Before the Friction Match

scenes.text: The lighter came first. The match came later.
In 1823, a German chemist named Döbereiner built a lighter the size of a lamp.
Inside, zinc sat in acid, making hydrogen gas. Turn a valve, and the gas flowed out.
It hit a tiny piece of platinum, which made the hydrogen burst into flame. No spark needed.
Three years later, in 1826, an English chemist scraped a coated stick and invented the friction match.
So when someone strikes a match, they're using the newer invention.

description:
The first lighter, Döbereiner's lamp, was built in 1823: hydrogen made from zinc and acid flowed onto a platinum catalyst and caught fire.
John Walker's friction match came in 1826, three years later, and went on sale in 1827.
Which invention would you have guessed came first?
first_comment: Did you guess the match came first? Which everyday invention do you think is older than it seems?
